REA coordinates the investigation

Frame one behavioral question, then inspect the matching artifact.

Retain the artifact identity, observations and unresolved questions.

For this client variant, use xdis for decoding and uncompyle6 for source recovery.
3   ·   Sources and qualifications in speaker notes

REA built-in inspect_python_pyc supports newer CPython variants, not this PyPy 2.7 artifact. These exhibits are real static fallback outputs, not claimed REA-native decompilation. All twelve functions decompiled with uncompyle6 3.9.3 and xdis 6.1.7 in an isolated tool directory.

title: Three views of the same function

text: Three views of the same function

Raw bytes show the actual co_code payload.

Disassembly resolves offsets, operations and operands.

Recovered Python reconstructs readable control flow from those operations.
4   ·   Sources and qualifications in speaker notes

The next exhibits show actual function bodies. A def line is reconstructed from the code object metadata. Original decorators, default argument expressions, comments and formatting are not recovered from an isolated code object.
A safe static recovery path

Read one archive member and limit its decompressed size.

Load the cross-version code object as data.

Decode instructions, then decompile a selected function.

Inspect the result without importing or calling the recovered module.
